messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing a small, deterministic resolution surface for rollout hints. Core idea: accept optional hints at multiple levels, resolve to a tiny runtime object, and emit a compact trace for observability.

sam: Drop the runtime shape so infra knows what to expect please.

maria: Runtime resolved shape: {effective_level, effective_weight, effective_origin, trace_id, resolution_reason}. Keep it minimal.

alex: Precedence rules? tie-breakers? also migration from legacy 'anchor' fields.

jamie: Suggest precedence: tenant_override (allow/block) > client > route > tenant-default > global. Tie-breaker: higher weight wins, then lexicographic origin id.

maria: Migration plan: map anchor -> tenant_override.allow, pin_strength -> weight (scaled); keep shim for 180 days and emit deprecation events.

lee: soft tenant_override: implement as weight-delta threshold (default 20). block = absolute veto. Add global safety cap for weight (0..1000).

alex: Observability: resolution_trace string <= 1024 bytes with applied_sources, final_weight, rule_id, clamped_fields. Redact PII unless sampled.

jamie: Metrics: gauge(effective_weight) per tenant, counter(override_mode_*), hist(resolution_latency_ms), sampled counter for full traces.

maria: Implementation note: expose pure function resolve(hints, overrides, legacy) -> resolved + trace. Property test and fuzz conflicting hints.

sam: Ops want a CLI to force re-resolve post-migration. Add `redwoodctl rollout resolve --tenant ID --force` with RBAC.

ops-bot: Will schedule a 3% dedicated canary post-merge, alert if reroute rate increases >0.5%.

maria: I'll open the RFC patch with schema, algorithm pseudocode, migration shim, metrics, tests, and examples (including TTL expiry example). Ping to review. :thumbsup:
